questions.question: Who defended the 100 m hurdles title and set a Championships record of 12.96 s at the Asian Athletics Championships in May 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jyothi Yarraji**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jyothi Yarraji** successfully defended her gold medal in the **women's 100 m hurdles** during the **Asian Athletics Championships** held in **May 2025**.
 
• She achieved a remarkable timing of **12.96 seconds**, which set a new **Championships record** for the event.
 
• By clocking **12.96 s**, she became the first woman in the history of the **Asian Athletics Championships** to dip below the previous record in this specific category, further cementing her dominance in **Asian hurdles**.
 
• This victory represents a significant **title defense**, as she had previously won the top spot in the earlier edition of the continental meet, proving her **consistency** and **elite form**.
 
• Her performance was a highlight for the **Indian contingent**, contributing to the nation's **gold medal tally** and securing her path toward global qualification standards.

• **Jyothi Yarraji:**
 
 
• She is a premier **Indian sprinter** specializing in the **100 m hurdles** and hails from **Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• She has been a consistent **national record holder** and was the first Indian woman to run the 100 m hurdles in under **13 seconds**.
 
• Her training is often supported by the **Reliance Foundation Athletics High-Performance Centre**, which has played a crucial role in her technical development.
 
 
 
• **Other Athletes Mentioned:**

• **Anu Raghavan:** A seasoned **400 m hurdles** specialist who has represented **India** at various international platforms, including the **Asian Games** and previous **Asian Championships**.
 
• **Pooja Singh:** A rising star in Indian athletics, primarily known for her achievements in the **High Jump** event rather than hurdles.
 
 
 
• **Asian Athletics Championships:**
 
 
• It is a **biennial** event organized by the **Asian Athletics Association**.
 
• The event serves as a platform for athletes from across **Asia** to compete for continental titles and gain **ranking points** for the **World Athletics Championships** and the **Olympic Games**.
 
• The **100 m hurdles** for women is a standard track event where athletes must clear **ten hurdles** of **83.8 cm** height over a 100-meter straight track.

questions.question: As of June 2025, how many times has the Indian men’s junior hockey team won the Junior Asia Cup?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Men’s Junior Hockey Team** has won the **Junior Asia Cup** a total of **5** times as of June 2025.
 
• India secured its **fifth title** in **December 2024** by defeating arch-rivals **Pakistan** with a score of **5-3** in the final held in **Muscat, Oman**.
 
• With this victory, India became the **most successful team** in the history of the tournament, surpassing Pakistan’s record of three titles.
 
• The five years in which India emerged as champions are **2004**, **2008**, **2015**, **2023**, and **2024**.
 
• In the **2024** edition, **Arshdeep Singh** was a standout performer, scoring a hat-trick in the final match to secure India's dominance in **Asian junior hockey**. ***Hence, the correct option is 5.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Men's Junior Asia Cup Overview**:
 
 
• The **Men's Junior Asia Cup** is an international **under-21** field hockey tournament organized by the **Asian Hockey Federation (AHF)**.
 
• The tournament was first held in **1988** in **Karachi, Pakistan**, where the hosts emerged as the inaugural champions.
 
• It serves as a primary **qualification tournament** for the **FIH Hockey Men's Junior World Cup**, with the top-ranked teams earning a spot on the global stage.
 
 
 
• **Tournament History and Rivalry**:
 
 
• **India** and **Pakistan** have been the most dominant forces in this competition. While **India** holds **5 titles**, **Pakistan** has won the trophy **3 times** (1988, 1992, and 1996).
 
• Other nations that have tasted success include **South Korea**, which won the tournament in **2000**.
 
• The **2023** edition was held in **Salalah, Oman**, where **India** defeated **Pakistan** **2-1** in the final to claim their fourth title.
 
 
 
• **Indian Hockey Development**:
 
 
• Success at the **Junior Asia Cup** is a testament to the robust **grassroots development** and **academy structures** in India, such as the **Odisha Naval Tata Hockey High Performance Centre**.
 
• Many players from the junior winning squads, such as **Harmanpreet Singh** (from the 2015 batch), have transitioned to become world-class players for the **Indian Senior National Team**.
 
• The **Government of India**, through the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports** and the **Sports Authority of India (SAI)**, provides extensive funding and training facilities for these young athletes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Host Nations**: **Oman** has become a frequent host for the tournament in recent years, successfully organizing both the **2023** and **2024** editions in **Salalah** and **Muscat** respectively.
 
• **Qualification Impact**: By reaching the final of the **2024 Junior Asia Cup**, India confirmed its berth for the **2025 FIH Hockey Men's Junior World Cup**.
 
• **Record Win Streak**: India’s victory in **2024** marked their **second consecutive title** win (2023 and 2024), demonstrating their current era of supremacy in the **under-21 category** across **Asia**.

questions.question: The ISSF World Cup is associated with which of the following sports?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shooting**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **ISSF World Cup** was introduced by the **International Shooting Sport Federation** in **1986**.
 
• The primary objective of establishing the **World Cup** was to provide a homogeneous system for qualification for the **Olympic Games** in shooting events.
 
• It comprises multiple stages held annually in different countries across the globe, featuring competitions in **Rifle**, **Pistol**, and **Shotgun** categories.
 
• The **ISSF World Cup Finals** are held at the end of the competition year, where the top-performing shooters of the season compete for the prestigious titles.
 
• The **International Shooting Sport Federation (ISSF)** is the governing body for Olympic shooting events and is headquartered in **Munich**, **Germany**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Shooting.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **International Shooting Sport Federation (ISSF):**
 
 
• The organization was founded in **1907** as the **International Shooting Union (UIT)** and later changed its name to **ISSF** in **1998**.
 
• It currently recognizes over **150** national shooting federations as members. The current President of the **ISSF** is **Luciano Rossi**, who took office in **December 2022**.
 
 
 
• **Swimming:**
 
 
• Swimming is globally governed by **World Aquatics** (formerly known as **FINA** - Fédération Internationale de Natation), which was founded in **1908**.
 
• Major international events include the **World Aquatics Championships** and the **FINA Swimming World Cup**, which is a series of short-course (**25m**) meets.
 
 
 
• **Squash:**
 
 
• Squash is governed by the **World Squash Federation (WSF)**, which is recognized by the **International Olympic Committee (IOC)**.
 
• The professional circuit is managed by the **Professional Squash Association (PSA)**, featuring the **PSA World Championships** as its pinnacle event.
 
 
 
• **Skiing:**
 
 
• Skiing events, including Alpine, Cross-Country, and Ski Jumping, are governed by the **International Ski and Snowboard Federation (FIS)**.
 
• The **FIS** was founded in **1924** during the first **Olympic Winter Games** in **Chamonix**, **France**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Shooting in the Olympics:** Shooting has been part of the **Modern Olympic Games** since the first edition in **Athens 1896**, except for the **1904** and **1928** editions.
 
• **India's Success:** **India** has a strong legacy in **ISSF** events. Notable athletes like **Abhinav Bindra** (the first Indian to win an individual **Olympic gold** in **2008**), **Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore**, **Gagan Narang**, and **Manu Bhaker** have brought international acclaim to the country in this sport.
 
• **ISSF World Championships:** Unlike the **World Cup** which is held **annually** with multiple stages, the **ISSF World Shooting Championships** are held every **four years** and are considered the most prestigious event after the **Olympics**.
 
• **Disciplines:** The **Rifle** and **Pistol** events are usually conducted at indoor or semi-outdoor ranges at distances of **10m**, **25m**, and **50m**, while **Shotgun** events (Skeet and Trap) take place at outdoor ranges.

questions.question: What was the Reserve Bank of India's repo rate in April 2025 after the 54th meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6.00%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **54th meeting** of the **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)** was conducted by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** in **April 2025** to review the prevailing macroeconomic conditions and determine the key policy rates for the **financial year 2025-26**.
 
• Following the deliberations of the committee, the **RBI** announced a reduction in the **policy repo rate**, bringing it down to **6.00%**. This decision represented a significant shift from the previous rate of **6.5%** which had been maintained for several preceding quarters.
 
• The reduction of **50 basis points** in the **repo rate** was aimed at stimulating **economic growth** and incentivizing investment by lowering the cost of borrowing for commercial banks and, subsequently, for businesses and individual consumers.
 
• Alongside the **repo rate**, the committee also adjusted the **Standing Deposit Facility (SDF)** rate to **5.75%** and the **Marginal Standing Facility (MSF)** rate to **6.25%**, maintaining the standard corridor width.
 
• The **MPC**, led by the **RBI Governor**, noted that while **inflation** was showing signs of stabilization within the target range, the move to **6.00%** was necessary to provide a cushion against global economic headwinds. ***Hence, the correct answer is 6.00%.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Repo Rate and Its Function:**
 
 
• The **Repo Rate** (Repurchase Option) is the **interest rate** at which the **Reserve Bank of India** lends money to commercial banks in the event of any shortfall of funds.
 
• It is used by **monetary authorities** to control **inflation**. When inflation is high, the **RBI** increases the repo rate to reduce **liquidity** in the economy; conversely, it lowers the rate to inject liquidity and spur **GDP growth**.
 
 
 
• **The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC):**
 
 
• The **MPC** is a statutory body constituted under the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**, following an amendment in **2016**.
 
• It consists of **6 members**: the **Governor of the RBI** (Chairperson, ex officio), the **Deputy Governor** in charge of monetary policy, one officer of the **RBI** nominated by the Central Board, and **three external members** appointed by the **Government of India**.
 
• The committee is mandated to meet at least **four times a year**, though it usually meets **bi-monthly** (six times a year) to publish the **Monetary Policy Report**.
 
 
 
• **Monetary Policy Stance:**
 
 
• The **MPC** often adopts specific "stances" such as **Accommodative** (aimed at growth), **Neutral** (no specific direction), or **Hawkish/Withdrawal of Accommodation** (aimed at curbing inflation).
 
• A rate cut to **6.00%** typically aligns with an **accommodative stance** to ensure that the **banking system** has enough liquidity to support credit flow.
 
 
 
• **Inflation Targeting:**
 
 
• The **Government of India**, in consultation with the **RBI**, sets a **Consumer Price Index (CPI)** inflation target.
 
• The current target is **4%** with a tolerance band of **+/- 2%**, meaning **inflation** should ideally remain between **2%** and **6%**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Standing Deposit Facility (SDF):** This replaced the **Reverse Repo Rate** as the floor of the **Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF)** corridor. It allows the **RBI** to absorb liquidity from banks without providing collateral.
 
• **Marginal Standing Facility (MSF):** A window for banks to borrow from the **RBI** in an emergency situation when inter-bank liquidity dries up completely. It is usually set **25 basis points** above the **Repo Rate**.
 
• **Basis Points (bps):** In finance, **100 basis points** equal **1%**. Therefore, a **50 bps** cut means a **0.50%** reduction in the rate.
</ul

• The medal tally consisted of **9 Gold**, **8 Silver**, and **10 Bronze** medals, showcasing India's dominance in various classifications of para-badminton.
 
• This stellar achievement placed **India** at the top of the medal table, ahead of traditional powerhouses like **China** and **Japan** in several categories.

• The **2025 edition** in **Thailand** saw participation from over **20 countries**, featuring various impairment groups including wheelchair and standing categories.
 
 
 
• **Classification in Para-Badminton**:
 
 
• Athletes are divided into **six classes**: **WH1** and **WH2** for wheelchair users, **SL3**, **SL4**, and **SU5** for standing players with limb impairments, and **SH6** for short stature athletes.

• **Recent Trends in Indian Para-Sports**:

• **Badminton Association of India (BAI)** and the **Paralympic Committee of India (PCI)** work in tandem to scout talent from **rural areas** and provide them with **international-standard training** facilities.

questions.question: In November 2025, 79 spotted deer were moved to which national park as part of conservation efforts in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandoli National Park**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **November 2025**, as part of a significant conservation initiative, **79 spotted deer** (also known as **Chital**) were successfully translocated to **Chandoli National Park** in **Maharashtra**.
 
• The primary objective of this relocation is to augment the **prey base** within the park, which is a critical component of the **Sahyadri Tiger Reserve (STR)**.
 
• This translocation project was executed by the **Maharashtra Forest Department** to ensure a sustainable population of herbivores, which is essential for the survival and potential reintroduction of large carnivores like **Tigers** in the region.
 
• The **79 spotted deer** were moved from overpopulated areas or zoological facilities, such as the **Rajiv Gandhi Zoological Park** in **Katraj, Pune**, to the wild habitat of **Chandoli**.
 
• The process involved advanced scientific methods for capture and transport to minimize stress and ensure the high survival rate of the animals during the **wildlife management** operation. ***Hence, the correct answer is Chandoli National Park.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chandoli National Park:**
 
 
• Located in the **Western Ghats**, it spans across the districts of **Sangli, Satara, Kolhapur, and Ratnagiri** in the state of **Maharashtra**.
 
• It was established as a **Wildlife Sanctuary** in **1985** and later declared a **National Park** in **May 2004**.
 
• In **2010**, it was merged with the **Koyna Wildlife Sanctuary** to form the **Sahyadri Tiger Reserve**, which is one of the few tiger reserves in the world located in a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.
 
• The park is home to diverse fauna, including the **Indian Bison (Gaur)**, **Leopards**, **Sloth Bears**, and various species of **deer** and **antelopes**.
 
 
 
• **Spotted Deer (Axis axis):**
 
 
• Commonly known as **Chital**, they are native to the **Indian subcontinent** and are characterized by their **golden-brown coat** with **white spots**.
 
• They play a vital role in the ecosystem as a primary **prey species** for major predators like **Tigers, Leopards, and Dholes**.
 
• They prefer **open grasslands** and **semi-evergreen forests**, making the habitat of **Chandoli** an ideal environment for their propagation.
 
 
 
• **Sahyadri Tiger Reserve (STR):**
 
 
• The reserve is unique due to its rugged terrain and **high-altitude evergreen forests**, providing a safe corridor for wildlife movement between the **northern and southern Western Ghats**.
 
• Recent conservation efforts have focused on habitat restoration and **prey-base enrichment** to make the reserve a viable home for **Big Cats**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Conservation Impact:** Increasing the number of herbivores like **spotted deer** helps in reducing **man-animal conflict** in peripheral areas by keeping predators within the protected forest boundaries.
 
• **Geographical Significance:** **Chandoli National Park** is located near the **Warna River** and includes the **Chandoli Dam**, which serves as a major water source for the local wildlife.
 
• **Other Options:** 
 
 
• **Sultanpur National Park** is a famous **bird sanctuary** located in **Haryana**.
 
• **Kaziranga National Park** in **Assam** is world-renowned for its **One-horned Rhinoceros**.
 
• **Keoladeo National Park** in **Rajasthan** is a premier **avifauna sanctuary** and a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which edition of the WHO Global Summit on Traditional Medicine will be held in New Delhi in December 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2nd Edition**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **World Health Organization (WHO)**, in collaboration with the **Ministry of Ayush**, will organize the **2nd WHO Global Summit on Traditional Medicine** in **New Delhi**.
 
• The summit is scheduled to be held in **December 2025**, serving as a major global platform to discuss the future of **Traditional, Complementary, and Integrative Medicine (TCIM)**.
 
• The primary objective of the **2025 Summit** is to build on the momentum generated during the inaugural event to further integrate traditional medicine into **national health systems** and global health policies.
 
• It aims to showcase **evidence-based traditional medicine** and foster international cooperation to meet the **United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)** related to health and well-being.
 
• India’s role as the host reinforces its position as a global hub for traditional healthcare practices like **Ayurveda, Yoga, and Unani**, supported by modern scientific validation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **1st WHO Global Summit on Traditional Medicine:**
 
 
• The first-ever global summit was held on **17-18 August 2023** in **Gandhinagar, Gujarat**, India.
 
• It was organized alongside the **G20 Health Ministers’ Meeting** under India’s **G20 Presidency**.
 
• The outcome document of this summit was the **Gujarat Declaration**, which committed to utilizing the potential of traditional medicine through **science, technology, and innovation**.
 
 
 
• **WHO Global Centre for Traditional Medicine (GCTM):**
 
 
• Established in **Jamnagar, Gujarat**, the **GCTM** is the first and only global outpost for traditional medicine by the **WHO**.
 
• The foundation stone was laid by Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** and WHO Director-General **Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus** in **April 2022**.
 
• It focuses on four main strategic areas: **Evidence and learning**, **Data and analytics**, **Sustainability and equity**, and **Innovation and technology**.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Ayush:**
 
 
• The **Ministry of AYUSH** was formed on **9th November 2014** to ensure the optimal development and propagation of **Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, and Homoeopathy**.
 
• The ministry plays a pivotal role in regulating the standards of education and research in traditional Indian medicine systems.
 
 
 
• **Global Importance of Traditional Medicine:**

questions.question: Which of the following bodies released the report titled ‘India’s Blue Economy: Strategy for Harnessing Deep-Sea and Offshore Fisheries’ in October 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**NITI Aayog**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The report titled **‘India’s Blue Economy: Strategy for Harnessing Deep-Sea and Offshore Fisheries’** was released by **NITI Aayog** in **October 2025**.
 
• The primary objective of this report is to provide a comprehensive roadmap for the **sustainable development** of India's maritime resources, specifically focusing on the untapped potential of **deep-sea fishing** and **offshore fisheries**.
 
• It highlights the strategic importance of the **Blue Economy** in achieving the goal of a **Viksit Bharat** (Developed India) by **2047**, emphasizing economic growth alongside environmental conservation.
 
• The document identifies critical gaps in the current fisheries sector, such as the lack of **advanced technology**, limited financial investment in **deep-sea vessels**, and the need for better **post-harvest infrastructure** like cold storage and processing units.
 
• Through this strategy, **NITI Aayog** aims to enhance the **livelihoods** of the coastal communities and increase the contribution of the **fisheries sector** to the national **GDP**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Blue Economy:**
 
 
• The term refers to the **sustainable use** of ocean resources for **economic growth**, improved livelihoods, and jobs while preserving the health of the ocean ecosystem.
 
• India has a vast coastline of approximately **7,517 km** and an **Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ)** spanning over **2.02 million square kilometers**, offering immense marine wealth.
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India):**
 
 
• Established on **January 1, 2015**, it serves as the premier **policy think tank** of the **Government of India**, replacing the erstwhile Planning Commission.
 
• It operates on the principle of **cooperative federalism** and provides strategic and technical advice to the central and state governments.
 
 
 
• **Relevant Organizations in the Sector:**
 
 
• **National Fisheries Development Board (NFDB):** Established in **2006** with headquarters in **Hyderabad**, it works under the **Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry, and Dairying** to enhance fish production.
 
• **Marine Products Export Development Authority (MPEDA):** Formed in **1972** under the **Ministry of Commerce and Industry**, it focuses on the **export** promotion of marine products from India.
 
 
 
• **Deep-Sea Fishing vs. Coastal Fishing:**
 
 
• **Coastal fishing** is generally limited to **12 nautical miles** from the shore, whereas **deep-sea fishing** involves operating in deeper waters, usually beyond the **continental shelf**, targeting species like **tuna** and **oceanic squids**.
 
• India's deep-sea resources remain underutilized because a majority of the **traditional fishing fleet** consists of small, motorized boats incapable of staying at sea for extended periods.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY):** This is a flagship scheme launched in **May 2020** to bring about a **Blue Revolution** through sustainable and responsible development of the fisheries sector with an investment of over **Rs. 20,000 crores**.
 
• **Employment Potential:** The fisheries sector in India provides **employment** to more than **28 million** people, particularly within marginalized **coastal communities**.
 
• **Global Standing:** India is currently the **third-largest** fish-producing country and the **second-largest** aquaculture nation in the world.
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDG):** The **Blue Economy** strategy aligns with **SDG 14**, which aims to "conserve and sustainably use the oceans, seas, and marine resources for sustainable development."
